scope: scripts/qualify_master_copy_tag_collision.py on a frozen Debug build of 5044285e (artifacts/oi1, git archive), 41/41 steps (run tc_531cbab9), in two owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 projects. Master-copy tag readback (1 November audit fix). Scratch 1: the table McTags with the Bool tags McProbe (%M60.0) and McSpare (%M61.0) became a master copy in the project library (library_create_master_copy, kind tagTable). Without a collision (both tags and McTags deleted first) library_instantiate (destinationComposition tagTables) applied with checkpoint, compile and save, and McTags read back with McProbe and McSpare under their own names. With a collision (McTags renamed to McTagsOld, so both tags stayed in the PLC root) TIA created the master copy's tags as McProbe(1) and McSpare(1): change_apply failed with MutationVerificationFailed (details renamedTags McProbe(1), McSpare(1), tagTable McTags) and change_status showed recovery_required with that failure; in a fresh empty owned Portal change_restore retrieved the project checkpoint to a new location (restored_to_new_locations), whose tag tables equalled those before the apply (McTagsOld with both tags, no McTags). Scratch 2: the unit CollUnit whose default tag table held the Bool tag UnitTag (%M70.0) became a master copy (kind softwareUnit); software_unit_create_from with onNameConflict=rename into the same PLC as CollUnit2: TIA created the copy's tag as UnitTag(1) beside CollUnit's UnitTag, and change_apply failed after the compile with MutationVerificationFailed naming UnitTag(1); change_restore in the applying Portal restored the checkpoint and the tag tables equalled those before the apply.
limitations: Owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN V4.1 projects; master copies in the project library only, Bool tags at bit-memory addresses. The tag-table collision is within the PLC root scope; the unit copy is within its own PLC with onNameConflict=rename (MasterCopyMode.Rename).

TIA's rename is recognized by its <name>(<n>) pattern against the names before the create, conservatively: a master-copy tag that is itself named <existing>(<n>) also fails the readback. User constants share the check but are not exercised.
Whether software_unit_create_from with MasterCopyMode.ThrowIfExists also renames a tag that exists in another unit or the PLC root is not exercised.
